title: Across Theorems: main_theorem via lemma1, lemma2
intent: Replace a single theorem `main_theorem : A = C` held by a `sorry` with two named helper lemmas `lemma1 : A = B` and `lemma2 : B = C`, and a parent whose entire proof is the two-step rewrite chain `rw [lemma1, lemma2]`. Each remaining hole is a smaller equality than the original, and the parent closes the moment both helpers are filled.

parent.name: main_theorem
parent.statement:
theorem main_theorem : A = C := by
  rw [lemma1, lemma2]

children.name: lemma1
children.statement: theorem lemma1 : A = B := by sorry
children.closed_by: sorry (a placeholder hole, left unfilled by design)

children.name: lemma2
children.statement: theorem lemma2 : B = C := by sorry
children.closed_by: sorry (a placeholder hole, left unfilled by design)

applicability.goal_shape: An equality A = C (or any rewrite-friendly relation) that factors through an intermediate B as A = B then B = C; the parent is closed by rw [lemma1, lemma2].
applicability.use_when: the direct proof is missing (a single sorry) and an intermediate value B makes each link a smaller, self-contained equality that can be stated as its own named lemma, so rw can rewrite by name.
applicability.avoid_when: the intermediate B does not reduce either side (children no smaller than the parent); the helper lemmas need hypotheses or local context that a bare rw cannot supply; or the equality is already a single rewrite step.

claims.claim: The parent main_theorem's entire proof is the single line rw [lemma1, lemma2], so A = C is closed from exactly the two children lemma1 and lemma2.
The decomposition's shape is direct_lemmas = 2 and depth = 1 (lemma1 and lemma2 are leaves, neither uses the other), with a one-line glue rw [lemma1, lemma2] and one line per helper.

consequences: The two helper statements must typecheck even while `sorry` (Lean treats `sorry` as an axiom, so the file shows no error but also no proof). The two lemmas must share the same intermediate B and the right orientation: `rw [lemma1, lemma2]` rewrites A to B then B to C, so `lemma1 : B = A` or a mismatched middle value breaks the chain. The move leaves the proof incomplete by design — the skill forbids declaring done while any `sorry` remains (line 93) — so the real work is deferred to filling lemma1 and lemma2.
